editorial:
You meet Fred and Mick, two old friends spending their days at a fancy Swiss Alps resort, talking about life, aging, and what comes next. Fred is a retired composer who refuses to pick up his baton again, even when his daughter Lena begs him. Mick is a filmmaker racing to finish one last script for his longtime muse Brenda. Alongside them is Jimmy, a young actor struggling to find meaning in his next role. The movie feels like a slow, beautiful daydream, full of quiet conversations, stunning mountain views, and strange little moments that stick with you.

The acting is the real draw here. Michael Caine and Harvey Keitel share an easy, lived-in chemistry, and Jane Fonda steals her short scenes with sharp energy. The pacing is slow and reflective, so if you want fast action, this is not your pick. But if you enjoy thoughtful stories about getting older, friendship, and art, you will find a lot to love. Stream it in 4K Ultra HD on Prime Video, rent on Apple TV, or grab the 4K Blu-ray for the best picture.
endingExplained: In the final scenes, Brenda arrives and bluntly rejects Mick's script, telling him his best days are behind him. Heartbroken, Mick jumps from his hotel balcony to his death. Meanwhile, Fred finally agrees to conduct his famous Simple Songs in a wide alpine meadow, with an orchestra and his daughter Lena watching. As the music swells, Lena is moved to tears, and Fred finds peace and purpose again, closing the film on a note of quiet hope.
targetAudience: Ideal for anyone who loves thoughtful stories about aging, friendship, and art.
